llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed cloud image-generation integration, with the main caveat that generic trigger phrases could route ordinary image requests to dLazy.

dimensions.detail: The CLI reads and uploads local files only when paths are supplied as media inputs, may download outputs only when requested, and uses the declared dLazy cloud endpoints; this is proportionate for a hosted image tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install path is a pinned npm package, `@dlazy/cli@1.2.3`, with an npx alternative, declared provenance, and no package install scripts observed in the inspected package metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent instructions are limited to using `dlazy banana2` and handling common auth/balance errors, but the trigger keywords include generic image-generation phrases that could activate the skill when the user did not name dLazy or Nano Banana.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Authentication persistence is disclosed: the CLI can save a dLazy API key under `~/.dlazy/config.json` and cache manifests/session metadata under the same directory. No background worker or auto-start persistence was observed.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is Nano Banana 2.0 image generation/editing, and its documented behavior matches that purpose: prompts and selected media inputs are sent to dLazy APIs and generated outputs are returned from dLazy-hosted URLs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable using dLazy as a cloud image-generation provider. Prompts and any local image paths you pass can be uploaded to dLazy, and `dlazy login` stores an API key locally; use the npx form or per-run `DLAZY_API_KEY` if you want less local persistence. Because the triggers are generic, confirm the agent is using dLazy/Nano Banana intentionally for broad image requests.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The English trigger list is broad for an image-generation skill and should be narrowed for better routing, but the artifact discloses the cloud API use, local-file upload behavior, and intended CLI command, so this is guidance rather than a Review-level concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese trigger list has the same broad-routing issue. It does not show hidden execution, purpose-mismatched behavior, or undisclosed data handling.
